tasks.short: Obtain missing information from policyholders and other people involved in a claim or application.

steps.what: Identify missing evidence in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.
Draft a specific information request in {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Missing information list, approved request template and contact preferences.
loop.output: A request explaining exactly which evidence is needed.
loop.check: Check required items, recipient, approved wording and absence of unrelated personal information.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; use the approved template if checks fail.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle routine requests; unusual evidence gaps need a short explanation in plain language.

steps.what: Check the recipient and send the information request through {EMAIL}.
Discuss unclear or sensitive information with the policyholder by phone.
Record responses and evidence in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.

loop.input: Written responses, attachments and clerk-authored call notes.
loop.output: Proposed evidence fields with source references and unresolved gaps.
loop.check: Validate field formats and source passages; distinguish customer statements from verified facts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per response; unresolved fields stay blank for review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured replies map directly; letters and call notes express the same facts in different ways.

tasks.design: Configure evidence checklists and reminders in the {OTHER} insurance administration system or {WORKFLOW}. A bounded drafting loop prepares requests in {EMAIL}; the clerk approves sending and handles sensitive calls through {TELEPHONY}. Reviewed responses update the evidence pack in {DOCS} and the case record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence requirements vary by claim type, and replies arrive across letters, attachments and calls.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurable checklists and inexpensive integrations cover routine gaps; bounded extraction and drafting handle the remaining free text.
tasks.still_hard: Identity checks, conflicting accounts, distress and inaccessible evidence still require personal contact. GDPR limits which information may be requested and shared.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise confusion or distress, ask proportionate follow-up questions and avoid treating an incomplete answer as an unwilling customer.

ambition.what: An assisted evidence appointment for policyholders who cannot complete written requests.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time composing reminders and copying replies. Within existing authority, they can choose an assisted appointment or escalate an evidence dispute; settlement authority does not expand.

reach.task: Plan assisted-contact appointments and balance callback capacity.
reach.learn: Queue forecasting, accessibility needs and escalation capacity.

evidence.claim: Paperbox organises insurance emails and attachments into case files; this supports intake feasibility, not autonomous customer conversations.
VKG reports automation of over 60% of claims correspondence; the result is a vendor case and is not a forecast here.
Rules, request templates and bounded drafting can reduce preparation while sensitive conversations remain human.

assumptions: The setting is a mid-size European insurer or insurance administrator with delegated clerical processing.
The {OTHER} slot denotes the insurance policy and claims administration system.
The supplied workflow list has no insurance claims workflow, so insurance case steps use other.
Time shares and remaining-time percentages are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Build ranges cover one initial claim type and include access review and any employee consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Available evidence checklists, contact permissions and secure submission channels.
Actual share of sensitive calls versus routine written follow-ups.
Access to case records and permitted processing of health information.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Which request wording produces complete replies without collecting unnecessary information?
How reliably can extraction distinguish a customer statement from independently verified evidence?
new_work: Review drafted requests and proposed evidence fields.
Handle failed deliveries, conflicting responses and overdue evidence.
Maintain checklists, templates and contact preferences.
Sample whether assisted-contact customers receive equivalent service.

tasks.short: Check policy wording and claim facts to establish coverage or refer uncertain findings.

steps.what: Retrieve the applicable policy version from the {OTHER} insurance administration system.
Check dates, insured risks and limits in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.
Read exclusions and endorsements in {DOCS} against the incident evidence.

loop.input: Version-locked policy clauses, incident evidence and standard rule results.
loop.output: A draft comparison of disputed facts and relevant clauses, with citations and uncertainty.
loop.check: Verify every clause citation and factual reference; flag ambiguity and missing evidence without inferring coverage.
loop.stop: One comparison and one citation-repair attempt; conflicting or unsupported conclusions go to a handler.
loop.why_not_simpler: Approved rules handle standard conditions; unusual wording and factual ambiguity need contextual reading.

steps.what: Record findings and referrals in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.
Approve ambiguous or adverse findings in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.

tasks.design: The {OTHER} insurance administration system retrieves the effective policy version and applies approved coverage rules. A bounded reading loop compares exceptional wording and evidence from {DOCS}, then an artefact generator records the cited recommendation and referral. An authorised handler approves ambiguous or adverse findings before they become effective.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy versions, endorsements and incident facts were difficult to join reliably, and exceptional wording resisted fixed rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned rules cover standard conditions; source-linked reading can prepare the exceptional comparison at lower cost.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed facts, legal interpretation and outdated rule mappings remain expensive. Significant solely automated decisions need an Article 22 assessment, including applicable exceptions and safeguards; a later review offer alone does not establish lawfulness.
tasks.human_edge: Interpret ambiguity fairly, recognise when evidence is insufficient and explain a defensible coverage decision.

ambition.what: A daily review of unresolved coverage referrals before they delay the claim.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time investigating disputed facts and less time searching policy versions. They can prioritise referral preparation, while binding coverage authority stays within existing delegation.

reach.task: Analyse recurring coverage referrals and propose clearer decision paths.
reach.learn: Rule traceability, exception analysis and separation of policy ambiguity from missing evidence.

evidence.claim: Nationale-Nederlanden has documented rapid processing for some simple claims; this does not establish general coverage automation.
A vendor case reports automatic decisions for a restricted eligible motor-claims population, supporting narrow rule boundaries.
Article 22 requires assessing restrictions, exceptions and safeguards for significant solely automated decisions.
A cited reading aid can prepare exceptional coverage analysis without receiving decision authority.

assumptions: Standard checks use approved, versioned rules rather than model-generated coverage decisions.
The {OTHER} slot denotes the insurance policy and claims administration system.
Handler approval time is an average contribution across cases requiring referral.
Time shares and remaining-time percentages are hypotheses for a pilot.
Build ranges cover one policy family, including historical-version testing, access review and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Policy families, endorsement complexity and availability of historical wording.
Existing coverage rules and their approval history.
Permitted automation under the organisation's legal assessment.
Whether any proposed use includes life or health risk assessment or pricing.
research_questions: How accurately can retrieval select the wording effective on the incident date?
Can reviewers detect unsupported interpretations in a source-linked coverage comparison?
Which exception categories can be converted into approved deterministic rules?
new_work: Validate rule mappings whenever policy wording changes.
Review exceptional comparisons and approve adverse findings.
Test historical policy versions and contradictory evidence.
Maintain decision traces and routes for human intervention and contest.

tasks.short: Validate incoming applications and claims, obtain required approvals, and create accurate insurance records.

steps.what: Sort applications, claim forms and attachments arriving through {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Incoming forms, email text and supporting documents.
loop.output: A classified intake pack with extracted fields and source locations.
loop.check: Validate schema, document counts, field formats and source evidence; quarantine unreadable or unsafe attachments.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unresolved items enter the clerk's queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured forms map directly; variable attachments and free-text notices need bounded reading.

steps.what: Match the intake to customers and policies in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.
Check forms and supporting evidence in {DOCS} for completeness and consistency.
Resolve clerical exceptions in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.
Approve referred policy issuance using the supporting documents in {DOCS}.
Create the policy or claim record in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.
Send the approved policy documents or claim receipt through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: A reusable intake schema accepts structured submissions and uses bounded extraction for residual documents in {EMAIL} and {DOCS}. Rules match records, check completeness and route exceptions through {WORKFLOW}; approved instructions create records in the {OTHER} insurance administration system with duplicate prevention and an audit trail. Configured templates send policy documents or claim receipts only after the required processing authority is established.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mixed document formats, uncertain customer matches and fragile record interfaces made straight-through processing expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing validation features, reusable connectors and bounded extraction reduce the cost of joining intake to record creation.
tasks.still_hard: Issuing a policy can create contractual obligations. Reliable authorisation, identity matching, transaction recovery and special-category data controls need careful implementation; registering a claim does not approve settlement.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve contradictory evidence and recognise when a clerical correction would become an unauthorised insurance decision.

ambition.what: A pre-submission completeness check for broker-submitted applications.

tasks.altitude: The clerk manages exception queues and helps submitters fix recurring errors. They gain control over queue sequencing and completeness support within delegated limits, without acquiring underwriting or settlement rights.

reach.task: Specify insurance intake mappings and transaction acceptance criteria.
reach.learn: Field lineage, duplicate prevention, authorisation checks and recovery after partial failure.

evidence.claim: Paperbox supports organising insurance correspondence and attachments into cases.
PostNL offers scanning and conversion of physical business forms into data.
Shift Claims offers claims triage and automation; this establishes available capability, not suitability for every policy transaction.
Authorised record creation, duplicate checks and template notices can use deterministic workflows.

assumptions: The {OTHER} slot denotes the insurance policy and claims administration system.
Existing approval matrices distinguish claim registration, pre-authorised issuance and referred policy issuance.
The approval branch applies only when required; its time share is averaged across the task mix.
Routine posting and delivery require valid prior authority and verified recipient details.
Time shares and remaining-time percentages are pilot hypotheses.
Build ranges cover one application type and one claim type, including access, rollout and any consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Current transaction interfaces, supported imports and existing configurable features.
Submission volumes, document languages and exception rates.
Which policy actions are already authorised before clerical processing.
Permitted recipient verification and delivery channels.
Applicable employee consultation requirements and access lead times.
research_questions: Which intake fields can be obtained directly from structured submissions?
What matching rules minimise false customer or policy associations?
Can interrupted posting be retried without creating duplicate policies or claims?
new_work: Review low-confidence extraction and matching exceptions.
Maintain field mappings, approval matrices and notice templates.
Reconcile submitted, posted and delivered transaction counts.
Investigate partial failures and sample completed records.

tasks.short: Enter, retrieve, organise and reconcile detailed insurance office records.

steps.what: Find requested records in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.
Copy insurance administration fields from {OTHER} into a tracking workbook in {SPREADSHEET}.
Name, link and file supporting documents in {DOCS}.
Resolve conflicting entries in the {OTHER} insurance administration system.
Apply archive categories and retention labels in {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Configure saved searches, case identifiers and document metadata in the {OTHER} insurance administration system and {DOCS}. Replace duplicate tracking in {SPREADSHEET} with a live records view, and use deterministic checks to prepare conflicts for the clerk. Retention labels follow approved schedules and legal holds, with exceptions routed through {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Disconnected search, inconsistent identifiers and local trackers created repeated entry and uncertainty about the authoritative record.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing search and metadata features often cover most of the task; small integrations can join identifiers and replace duplicate trackers.
tasks.still_hard: Historic duplicates, disputed corrections and missing source documents require investigation. Retention periods, legal holds and access restrictions need locally validated rules.
tasks.human_edge: Establish which source is authoritative and explain corrections without silently overwriting a contested history.

ambition.what: A permission-aware self-service case-document index for authorised office colleagues.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time locating and copying records and more time resolving conflicts. They can make documented clerical corrections within existing limits; disputed ownership and retention decisions remain escalations.

reach.task: Design a shared case index and maintain consistent record categories.
reach.learn: Metadata standards, permission-aware search, retention schedules and legal holds.

reach.task: Identify recurring causes of conflicting insurance records.
reach.learn: Data lineage and analysis of correction patterns.

evidence.claim: Saved searches, metadata, controlled updates and retention labels are established records-management capabilities.
Paperbox demonstrates insurance correspondence organisation, relevant to linking documents to cases.
The documented public-health spreadsheet failure illustrates the risk of relying on unchecked workbook capacity.

assumptions: This insurance role mainly handles office records; warehouse records are outside the typical task.
The {OTHER} slot denotes the insurance policy and claims administration system.
A local workbook duplicates fields already held in the authoritative record.
Source documents carry usable case identifiers; free-text indexing is not needed in the initial build.
Automatic archiving applies labels and access rules; it does not introduce automatic permanent deletion.
Time shares and remaining-time percentages are estimates. Build ranges include access validation and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Whether duplicate workbooks exist and what additional information they contain.
Available search, metadata and retention configuration.
Historical data quality, access boundaries and legal hold arrangements.
research_questions: Which records features can replace local tracking without custom code?
Can a shared index preserve all existing document access restrictions?
Which conflict checks identify actionable discrepancies without overwhelming clerks?
new_work: Maintain identifiers, metadata and saved views.
Resolve conflict queues and document correction rationales.
Check archive exceptions and legal hold propagation.
Review permissions when roles or document categories change.

role.altitude: The week shifts from searching, copying and chasing toward evidence support, record conflicts and coverage referrals. The clerk gains practical control over queue priorities and clerical corrections within existing delegation; underwriting, adverse coverage and settlement authority require separate authorisation.
reach: Administrative services manager: plan assisted-contact capacity.
Management analyst: investigate recurring evidence gaps and coverage referrals.
Computer systems analyst: specify mappings, authorisation checks and recovery behaviour.
File clerk: improve case indexing, permissions and retention categories.
skills_to_grow: Translate approved procedures into testable completeness and routing rules.
Verify source-linked extraction and distinguish statements from established facts.
Trace policy versions, endorsements and evidence provenance.
Handle sensitive conversations and accessible evidence collection.
Understand transaction recovery, access control and exception queues.
Recognise GDPR decision safeguards and relevant national consultation requirements.
role.ambitious_version: Run an evidence-readiness service combining pre-submission checks, assisted evidence appointments and early coverage referrals. Start with reusable templates, schemas and approved exports; connect live records when access is available. Keep significant insurance decisions within explicit delegated authority.

job.title: Insurance Claims and Policy Processing Clerks
